claim: G-baToN relies upon nanobody-directed fluorescent protein transfer to enable sensitive and specific labeling of cells after cell-cell interactions.
source: Here, we describe GFP-based Touching Nexus (G-baToN) which relies upon nanobody-directed fluorescent protein transfer to enable sensitive and specific labeling of cells after cell-cell interactions.
evidence: The abstract directly states this as a description of the system's mechanism.

claim: G-baToN is a generalizable system that enables physical contact-based labeling between various human and mouse cell types.
source: G-baToN is a generalizable system that enables physical contact-based labeling between various human and mouse cell types, including endothelial cell-pericyte, neuron-astrocyte, and diverse cancer-stromal cell pairs.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states the system's generalizability across multiple cell types with specific examples.

claim: Cell-cell interactions contribute to almost all physiological and pathological states.
source: Cell-cell interactions contribute to almost all physiological and pathological states (Deb, 2014; Komohara and Takeya, 2017; Konry et al., 2016; Zhang and Liu, 2019).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to prior literature.

claim: The extent to which cell-cell interactions influence cell state, drive heterogeneity, and enable proper tissue function remains poorly understood.
source: Despite the explosion of interest in uncovering and understanding cellular heterogeneity in tissues and across disease states, the extent to which cell-cell interactions influence cell state, drive heterogeneity, and enable proper tissue function remains poorly understood (Konry et al., 2016; Tsioris et al., 2014; Zhang and Liu, 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations indicating a gap in current knowledge.

claim: Interactions between cancer cells and stromal cells play central roles in cancer initiation, progression, and metastasis.
source: Interactions between cancer cells and stromal cells play central roles in cancer initiation, progression, and metastasis (Kitadai, 2010; Orimo and Weinberg, 2006).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: The impact of direct physical interactions between cancer cells and stromal cells remains understudied.
source: While secreted factors relaying pro- or anti-tumorigenic signals have been extensively investigated, the impact of direct physical interactions between cancer cells and stromal cells remains understudied (Bendas and Borsig, 2012; Dittmer and Leyh, 2014; Nagarsheth et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations and contrasts with the state of research on secreted factors.

claim: Endogenous cell-cell interactions can result in transfer of surface proteins between cells through trans-endocytosis or trogocytosis.
source: Endogenous cell-cell interactions can result in transfer of surface proteins between cells, mainly through either trans-endocytosis or trogocytosis (Langridge and Struhl, 2017; Li et al., 2019; Ovcinnikovs et al., 2019).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: Co-culturing sGFP sender cells with αGFP receiver cells led to GFP transfer and labeling of the receiver cells.
source: Co-culturing sGFP sender cells with αGFP receiver cells led to GFP transfer and labeling of the receiver cells (Figure 1A,B and Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in the referenced figures.

claim: Receiver cell labeling required direct cell-cell contact.
source: Receiver cell labeling required direct cell-cell contact, active membrane dynamics, and pairing between sGFP and its cognate αGFP receptor (Figure 1C,D and Figure 1—figure supplement 1B, C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data including transwell experiments shown in the referenced figures.

claim: sGFP transfer was accompanied by reduced GFP on the sender cells.
source: Notably, sGFP transfer was accompanied by reduced GFP on the sender cells, downregulation of αGFP from the surface of the receiver cells and was partially blocked by chemical inhibitors of endocytosis – all consistent with active GFP transfer and internalization into receiver cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 1D–F).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in the referenced figures.

claim: GFP transfer could be detected within five minutes of co-culture.
source: GFP transfer could be detected within five minutes of co-culture and was half-maximal after 6 hr (Figure 1F and Figure 1—figure supplement 1G-H).
evidence: This claim is supported by time-course experimental data shown in the referenced figures.

claim: GFP fluorescence in receiver cells decayed rapidly after isolation of touched receiver cells from sender cells.
source: Importantly, GFP fluorescence in receiver cells decayed rapidly after isolation of touched receiver cells from sender cells, thus documenting the transient labeling of receiver cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 1I).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing fluorescence decay over time.

claim: The fraction of labeled receiver cells was proportional to the number of sender cells.
source: The fraction of labeled receiver cells was proportional to the number of sender cells, and even the addition of very few sender cells (representing less than one sender cell to 105 receiver cells) was sufficient to label rare receiver cells (Figure 1G,H).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing dose-response relationship.

claim: The VEGFR2 transmembrane domain enabled the highest transfer efficiency, resulting in about a threefold increase relative to the original design.
source: The VEGFR2 transmembrane domain enabled the highest transfer efficiency, resulting in about a threefold increase relative to the original design (Figure 2A–C).
evidence: This claim is supported by comparative experimental data shown in the referenced figures.

claim: The efficiency of GFP transfer correlated with GFP affinity.
source: Overall, the efficiency of GFP transfer correlated with GFP affinity.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion drawn from the nanobody affinity experiments.

claim: The PDGFR transmembrane domain minimized bidirectional transfer.
source: The PDGFR transmembrane domain minimized bidirectional transfer and thus was the optimal design for minimizing retrograde transfer which could generate false-positive signals (Figure 2G–I).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data comparing different transmembrane domains.

claim: Co-culturing sGFP-expressing lung adenocarcinoma cells with primary human umbilical vein endothelial cells in a 2D format led to robust endothelial cell labeling.
source: Co-culturing sGFP-expressing lung adenocarcinoma cells with primary human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVECs) in a 2D format led to robust endothelial cell labeling (Figure 3A,B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in the referenced figures.

claim: Within 3D microfluidic chips, pre-seeded HUVECs expressing αGFP were robustly labeled following co-incubation with sGFP-expressing lung adenocarcinoma cells.
source: Additionally, within 3D microfluidic chips, pre-seeded HUVECs expressing αGFP were robustly labeled following co-incubation with sGFP-expressing lung adenocarcinoma cells (Figure 3E–G).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from 3D culture systems.

claim: αGFP-expressing CD4 and CD8 T cells that interacted with sGFP-expressing lung cancer cells in culture were specifically labeled.
source: αGFP-expressing CD4 and CD8 T cells that interacted with sGFP-expressing lung cancer cells in culture were specifically labeled (Figure 4A–C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from T cell co-culture experiments.

claim: Over 60% of αGFP-expressing CD4 T cells within the tumor-bearing lungs were labeled with GFP 24 hr after T cell transplantation.
source: 24 hr after T cell transplantation, over 60% of αGFP-expressing CD4 T cells within the tumor-bearing lungs were labeled with GFP, while control CD4 T cells remained unlabeled (Figure 4D,E).
evidence: This claim is supported by in vivo experimental data.

claim: Physical contact between cancer cells and neuronal axons led to punctate-like GFP granule transport into receiver neurons.
source: Physical contact between cancer cells and neuronal axons led to punctate-like GFP granule transport into receiver neurons (Figure 5A–B).
evidence: This claim is supported by imaging data from neuron co-culture experiments.

claim: Each receiver cell type was able to uptake GFP from sGFP-expressing lung cancer sender cells upon cell-cell contact.
source: Each receiver cell type was able to uptake GFP from sGFP-expressing lung cancer sender cells upon cell-cell contact (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data testing multiple cell types.

claim: Diverse cancer cell lines and primary cell types expressing sGFP were able to transfer GFP to αGFP-expressing HEK293 receiver cells.
source: Furthermore, diverse cancer cell lines and primary cell types expressing sGFP were able to transfer GFP to αGFP-expressing HEK293 receiver cells (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B–F).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data testing multiple sender cell types.

claim: Co-culturing sGFP-expressing HUVEC and αGFP-expressing primary human umbilical vein smooth muscle cells resulted in efficient receiver smooth muscle cell labeling.
source: Co-culturing sGFP-expressing HUVEC and αGFP-expressing primary human umbilical vein smooth muscle cells (HUVSMC) resulted in efficient receiver smooth muscle cell labeling (Figure 3C,D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from endothelial-smooth muscle cell co-cultures.

claim: sGFP-expressing astrocytes were able to transfer GFP to αGFP-expressing cortical neurons.
source: Furthermore, sGFP-expressing astrocytes were able to transfer GFP to αGFP-expressing cortical neurons (Figure 5C,D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from astrocyte-neuron co-cultures.

claim: Co-culture of surface BFP sender cells with αGFP receiver cells generated BFP-labeled receiver cells due to cross reactivity of αGFP with BFP.
source: Due to the cross reactivity of αGFP with BFP, co-culture of surface BFP (sBFP) sender cells with αGFP receiver cells generated BFP-labeled receiver cells (Fridy et al., 2014; Figure 6—figure supplement 1A, B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data and a citation explaining the cross-reactivity.

claim: Orthogonal systems consisting of surface-mCherry/αmCherry and surface-GCN4-GFP/αGCN4 led to efficient and specific receiver cell labeling.
source: Orthogonal systems consisting of surface-mCherry/αmCherry (LaM4)(Fridy et al., 2014) and surface-GCN4-GFP/αGCN4 (single-chain variable fragment, scFV)(Tanenbaum et al., 2014) also led to efficient and specific receiver cell labeling (Figure 6—figure supplement 1C–F).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data testing orthogonal labeling systems.

claim: Co-culture of cells expressing sGFP and αmCherry with cells expressing smCherry and αGFP resulted in reciprocal labeling of both interacting cell types.
source: Co-culture of cells expressing sGFP and αmCherry with cells expressing smCherry and αGFP resulted in reciprocal labeling of both interacting cell types (Figure 6A,B, and Figure 6—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data demonstrating bidirectional labeling.

claim: Co-expression of αmCherry and αGFP on receiver cells enabled dual color labeling of receiver cells that had interacted with smCherry-expressing, sGFP-expressing, or both sender cell types.
source: Specifically, co-expression of αmCherry and αGFP on receiver cells enabled dual color labeling of receiver cells that had interacted with smCherry-expressing, sGFP-expressing, or both sender cell types (Figure 6C,D, and Figure 6—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data demonstrating AND gate logic.

claim: Co-culture of Alexa Fluor 660-loaded sHalo-GFP sender cells with αGFP receiver cells enabled co-transfer of both GFP and AF660.
source: Co-culture of Alexa Fluor 660 (AF660)-loaded sHalo-GFP sender cells with αGFP receiver cells enabled co-transfer of both GFP and AF660 (Figure 7C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing dual transfer of protein and chemical fluorophore.

claim: Transfer of the chemical fluorophore using sHalo-GFP-based labeling of receiver cells led to increased signal-to-noise ratio and higher sensitivity compared to GFP.
source: Compared to GFP, transfer of the chemical fluorophore using sHalo-GFP-based labeling of receiver cells led to increased signal-to-noise ratio and higher sensitivity (Figure 7C,D).
evidence: This claim is supported by comparative experimental data.

claim: Changing from a protein (GFP) to a chemical fluorophore extended the half-life of labeling.
source: Importantly, changing from a protein (GFP) to a chemical fluorophore also extended the half-life of labeling, thus enabling partially tunable persistence of labeling after touching (Figure 7E).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing differential decay rates.

claim: The ratio of AF488 to AF660 transferred to the dually labeled receiver cells strongly correlated with the ratio of the two sGCN4-Halo sender populations within the co-culture.
source: Importantly, the ratio of AF488 to AF660 transferred to the dually labeled receiver cells strongly correlated with the ratio of the two sGCN4-Halo sender populations within the co-culture, suggesting that this system can quantitively measure higher order cell-cell interactions (Figure 7H).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing quantitative correlation.

claim: Co-culture of sGFP-tdTomato sender cells with αGFP receiver cells resulted in stoichiometric tdTomato and GFP transfer to receiver cells.
source: In addition to the co-transfer of Halo-Tag with sGFP, we also generated sender cells with surface expression of a GFP-tdTomato fusion protein (sGFP-Tom) and uncovered stoichiometric tdTomato and GFP transfer to αGFP receiver cells (Figure 8A,B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing co-transfer of fusion proteins.

claim: Co-culture of sGFP-PuroR sender cells with αGFP receiver cells led to moderate puromycin resistance of touched receiver cells.
source: We generated sGFP-PuroR-expressing sender cells and found that co-culture of sGFP-PuroR sender cells with αGFP receiver cells led to moderate puromycin resistance of touched receiver cells (Figure 8C,D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing functional cargo transfer.

claim: Loading of sGCN4-HaloTag sender cells with HaloTag-conjugated, AF647-coupled ssDNA prior to co-culture with αGCN4 receiver cells revealed successful co-transfer of fluorescently labeled ssDNA to receiver cells.
source: Finally, loading of sGCN4-HaloTag sender cells with HaloTag-conjugated, AF647-coupled ssDNA prior to co-culture with αGCN4 receiver cells revealed successful co-transfer of fluorescently labeled ssDNA to receiver cells (Figure 8E–G).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing DNA cargo transfer.

claim: The G-baToN system can record diverse cell-cell interactions in a specific and sensitive manner.
source: Here, we developed and optimized a novel cell-cell interaction reporter system and showed that this G-baToN system can record diverse cell-cell interactions in a specific and sensitive manner.
evidence: This is a summary statement in the Discussion supported by all the experimental data presented.

claim: The ability of diverse primary cell types to serve as both sender and receiver cells suggests that the G-baToN system is generalizable.
source: Our data document the ability of diverse primary cell types to serve as both sender and receiver cells, suggesting that the G-baToN system is not only simple, sensitive and rapid, but also generalizable.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data showing multiple cell types can use the system.

claim: Multicolor derivatives of G-baToN enable qualitative and quantitative analyses of higher order interactions involving more than two cell types.
source: Multicolor derivatives of G-baToN enable qualitative and quantitative analyses of higher order interactions involving more than two cell types.
evidence: This is a summary statement supported by the multicolor labeling experiments.

claim: The G-baToN system labels receiver cells through transfer of cell surface GFP which ensures only transient labeling due to its lability.
source: The G-baToN system labels receiver cells through transfer of cell surface GFP which, due to its lability, ensures only transient labeling.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by the GFP decay experiments.

claim: Using chemical fluorophores significantly extends label persistence within receiver cells compared to GFP.
source: Conversely, we have shown that using chemical fluorophores significantly extends label persistence within receiver cells (Figure 7E), which can be used for longer term labeling of receiver cells that undergo dynamic interactions.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data comparing GFP and chemical fluorophore decay rates.

claim: The G-baToN system relies on cell surface ligand-receptor recognition.
source: As with other cell-cell interaction reporter systems, the G-baToN system relies on cell surface ligand-receptor recognition (Supplementary files 1–2).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as a characteristic of the system.

claim: G-baToN systems could stabilize normal cell-cell interactions due to exogenous ligand-receptor pairs.
source: Consequently, these systems could stabilize normal cell-cell interactions.
evidence: This is a potential limitation discussed by the authors based on the system design.

claim: Transferred cargo proteins may be able to modify receiver cell signaling or promote cell death.
source: Transferred cargo proteins may be able to modify receiver cell signaling or promote cell death.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about potential applications based on the cargo transfer capability.

claim: GFP protein is transferred to receiver cells, not just fluorescence signal.
source: Western blot analysis of FACS purified Control and αGFP receiver 293 cells cultured in isolation or co-culture with sGFP Tomato-positive sender cells (mouse KPT lung cancer cells) for 24 hr. sGFP but not Tomato is present in touched αGFP receiver cells.
evidence: Western blot data in Figure 1—figure supplement 1a demonstrates protein transfer.

claim: GFP cannot be transferred from fixed sGFP sender cells to live αGFP receiver cells.
source: GFP cannot be transferred from fixed sGFP sender cells to live αGFP receiver cells. sGFP sender cells were fixed in 1% PFA for 5 min and washed with PBS before co-cultured with αGFP receiver cells at a 1:1 ratio for 24 hr.
evidence: Experimental data shows that fixed cells cannot transfer GFP, indicating active process requirement.

claim: GFP transfer to receiver cells is accompanied by a reduction of GFP on the sender cells.
source: GFP transfer to receiver cells is accompanied by a reduction of GFP on the sender cells. GFP expression on sender cells after 24 hr co-culture with control or αGFP-expressing 293 receiver cells at a 1:1 ratio. Co-culture with αGFP expressing but not control receiver cells reduced GFP on sGFP sender cells.
evidence: Flow cytometry data shows decreased GFP on sender cells after co-culture with αGFP receivers.

claim: GFP transfer is accompanied with αGFP internalization on receiver cells.
source: GFP transfer is accompanied with αGFP internalization on receiver cells. Analysis of surface αGFP (Myc-tag) on 293 receiver cell co-cultured for 24 hr with sGFP sender cells.
evidence: Flow cytometry data shows decreased surface αGFP after co-culture with sGFP senders.

claim: GFP transfer to receiver cells is partially dependent on membrane dynamics of endocytosis.
source: GFP transfer to 293 receiver cells is partially dependent on membrane dynamics of endocytosis. Both a clathrin inhibitor (Pitstop, 20 μM) and a dynamin inhibitor (Dyngo 4a, 10 μM) partially inhibit GFP transfer from sGFP sender cells to αGFP receiver cells.
evidence: Chemical inhibitor experiments demonstrate partial dependence on endocytic machinery.

claim: A shift in GFP MFI was detected 5 min after mixing sGFP sender cells with αGFP receiver cells.
source: GFP transfer to αGFP 293 receiver cells can be very rapid. A shift in GFP MFI was detected 5 min after mixing sGFP sender cells with αGFP receiver cell.
evidence: Flow cytometry time course data shows rapid GFP transfer within 5 minutes.

claim: GFP in receiver cells has a half-life of approximately 2 hours after removal of sender cells.
source: Rapid GFP degradation in touched receiver cells after removal of the sGFP sender cells. After 6 hr co-culture, GFP-positive receiver cells were purified by FACS followed by culture without sender cells. Receiver cells were defined as mCherrynegPInegBFPpos cells. GFP MFI in receiver cells reduced rapidly (T1/2 approximately 2 hr).
evidence: Time course data after FACS purification shows rapid GFP decay with calculated half-life.

claim: The G-baToN system adapted a synthetic ligand-receptor system based on surface GFP on sender cells and a cell surface anti-GFP nanobody on receiver cells.
source: To create a system in which a fluorescent signal could be transferred between neighboring cells, we adapted a synthetic ligand-receptor system based on the expression of surface GFP (sGFP) on sender cells and a cell surface anti-GFP (αGFP) nanobody on receiver cells (Fridy et al., 2014; Lim et al., 2013; Morsut et al., 2016).
evidence: This describes the design basis of the system with supporting citations.

claim: Receiver cell labeling required active membrane dynamics.
source: Receiver cell labeling required direct cell-cell contact, active membrane dynamics, and pairing between sGFP and its cognate αGFP receptor (Figure 1C,D and Figure 1—figure supplement 1B, C).
evidence: This is supported by experiments with fixed cells and endocytosis inhibitors.

claim: Receiver cell labeling required pairing between sGFP and its cognate αGFP receptor.
source: Receiver cell labeling required direct cell-cell contact, active membrane dynamics, and pairing between sGFP and its cognate αGFP receptor (Figure 1C,D and Figure 1—figure supplement 1B, C).
evidence: This is supported by experiments showing no transfer with mismatched receptors.

claim: sGFP transfer was partially blocked by chemical inhibitors of endocytosis.
source: Notably, sGFP transfer was accompanied by reduced GFP on the sender cells, downregulation of αGFP from the surface of the receiver cells and was partially blocked by chemical inhibitors of endocytosis – all consistent with active GFP transfer and internalization into receiver cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 1D–F).
evidence: Chemical inhibitor experiments demonstrate partial dependence on endocytosis.

claim: GFP transfer was half-maximal after 6 hr of co-culture.
source: GFP transfer could be detected within five minutes of co-culture and was half-maximal after 6 hr (Figure 1F and Figure 1—figure supplement 1G-H).
evidence: Time course experiments quantified the kinetics of GFP transfer.

claim: Even the addition of very few sender cells (representing less than one sender cell to 10^5 receiver cells) was sufficient to label rare receiver cells.
source: The fraction of labeled receiver cells was proportional to the number of sender cells, and even the addition of very few sender cells (representing less than one sender cell to 105 receiver cells) was sufficient to label rare receiver cells (Figure 1G,H).
evidence: Sensitivity experiments demonstrate detection of rare interactions.

claim: The transfer of GFP to αGFP-expressing cells is a rapid and sensitive method to mark cells that have physically interacted with a predefined sender population.
source: Thus, the transfer of GFP to αGFP-expressing cells is a rapid and sensitive method to mark cells that have physically interacted with a predefined sender population.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the kinetics and sensitivity experiments.

claim: The original G-baToN design used the Notch1 transmembrane domain to link the LaG17-αGFP nanobody onto the receiver cell surface.
source: We initially used a published sGFP-αGFP pair in which the Notch1 transmembrane domain links the LaG17-αGFP nanobody onto the receiver cell surface and the PDGFR transmembrane domain links sGFP onto the sender cell surface (Morsut et al., 2016).
evidence: This describes the initial design with a citation to the source.

claim: The original G-baToN design used the PDGFR transmembrane domain to link sGFP onto the sender cell surface.
source: We initially used a published sGFP-αGFP pair in which the Notch1 transmembrane domain links the LaG17-αGFP nanobody onto the receiver cell surface and the PDGFR transmembrane domain links sGFP onto the sender cell surface (Morsut et al., 2016).
evidence: This describes the initial design with a citation to the source.

claim: A minimal affinity was required for GFP transfer between nanobodies and GFP.
source: While nanobodies exhibiting the highest affinities performed similarly, we noted a minimal affinity required for GFP transfer (Figure 2F).
evidence: Experiments with different affinity nanobodies showed a threshold effect.

claim: The rate of retrograde transfer of αGFP-VEGFR2-BFP from receiver to sender cells was influenced by the sGFP transmembrane domain.
source: Lastly, permutation of the transmembrane domain of sGFP on the sender cell revealed that the rate of retrograde transfer of αGFP-VEGFR2-BFP from receiver to sender cells was influenced by the sGFP transmembrane domain (Figure 2G–I).
evidence: Experiments testing different transmembrane domains showed differential retrograde transfer.

claim: The G-baToN system is able to efficiently record cancer cell-endothelial cell interactions across multiple culture conditions.
source: Thus, the G-baToN system is able to efficiently record cancer cell-endothelial cell interactions across multiple culture conditions.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on experiments in 2D and 3D culture systems.

claim: The G-baToN system is capable of recording cancer cell-T cell interactions both in vitro and in vivo.
source: Thus, the G-baToN system is capable of recording cancer cell-T cell interactions both in vitro and in vivo.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on in vitro co-culture and in vivo transplantation experiments.

claim: G-baToN-based labeling extends beyond transformed cell types and can label diverse primary cell types in co-culture.
source: Thus, G-baToN-based labeling extends beyond transformed cell types and can label diverse primary cell types in co-culture.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on experiments with multiple primary cell types.

claim: Receiver cell labeling required sGFP-expression on the sender cell and αGFP expression on the receiver cells.
source: As anticipated, receiver cell labeling required sGFP-expression on the sender cell and αGFP expression on the receiver cells.
evidence: This is stated as a requirement demonstrated by control experiments throughout the paper.

claim: The results document the efficiency of G-baToN-based cell labeling across diverse cell types.
source: Collectively, these results document the efficiency of G-baToN-based cell labeling across diverse cell types.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on experiments with endothelial-smooth muscle and astrocyte-neuron interactions.

claim: The G-baToN labeling system can be extended to additional antigen/antibody pairs beyond GFP/αGFP.
source: Thus, the G-baToN labeling system can be extended to additional antigen/antibody pairs.
evidence: This conclusion is based on successful experiments with BFP, mCherry, and GCN4 systems.

claim: Engineering cells with orthogonal systems in an anti-parallel fashion enables reciprocal labeling of both interacting cells.
source: Engineering cells with these orthogonal systems in an anti-parallel fashion should enable reciprocal labeling of both interacting cells.
evidence: This is stated as a design principle and demonstrated experimentally.

claim: Derivatives of the G-baToN system allow for additional degrees of resolution of complex cell-cell interactions.
source: Thus, derivatives of the G-baToN system allow for additional degrees of resolution of complex cell-cell interactions.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on reciprocal and AND gate labeling experiments.

claim: Covalent attachment of a synthetic fluorophore to sHalo-GFP enabled specific loading onto sender cells.
source: Covalent attachment of a synthetic fluorophore to sHalo-GFP enabled specific loading onto sender cells (Figure 7B).
evidence: Experimental data shows specific labeling of HaloTag-expressing cells.

claim: Co-culture of AF660-loaded sHalo-GFP sender cells with αGFP receiver cells enabled co-transfer of both GFP and AF660.
source: Co-culture of Alexa Fluor 660 (AF660)-loaded sHalo-GFP sender cells with αGFP receiver cells enabled co-transfer of both GFP and AF660 (Figure 7C).
evidence: Flow cytometry data shows dual labeling of receiver cells with both fluorophores.

claim: baToN systems enable contact-dependent transport of different macromolecules between cells.
source: Thus, baToN systems enable contact-dependent transport of different macromolecules between cells.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on experiments transferring proteins, DNA, and small molecules.

claim: The simplicity of the G-baToN two-component system, combined with its generalizability across cell types, excellent foreground to background ratio, and rapid labeling, enables facile analysis of the dynamics of cellular interaction.
source: The simplicity of this two-component system, combined with its generalizability across cell types, excellent foreground to background ratio, and rapid labeling, should enable facile analysis of the dynamics of cellular interaction.
evidence: This is a summary statement of the system's advantages based on all experimental results.

claim: The ability to track physically interacting cells with these systems will greatly accelerate understanding of the outputs of cell-cell interactions in cancer and across many biological processes.
source: The ability to track physically interacting cells with these simple and sensitive systems will greatly accelerate our understanding of the outputs of cell-cell interactions in cancer as well as across many biological processes.
evidence: This is a forward-looking statement about the potential impact of the technology.

claim: Molecular methods to profile cell state largely fail to uncover the causal relationship between cell-cell interactions and the underlying biology.
source: Molecular methods to profile cell state, including in situ approaches within intact tissues, largely fail to uncover the causal relationship between cell-cell interactions and the underlying biology (Giladi et al., 2020; Halpern et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations indicating limitations of current methods.

claim: Modalities to capture cell-cell interactions are limited.
source: Computational and experimental methods to characterize cell-cell interactions yield additional layers of dimensionality; however, modalities to capture cell-cell interactions are limited (Boisset et al., 2018; Morsut et al., 2016; Pasqual et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations and describes a gap in available methods.

claim: The development of novel systems to detect and quantify cell-cell interactions will accelerate the mapping of the interaction networks of multicellular systems.
source: Much as diverse systems to detect and quantify protein-protein interactions have revolutionized our biochemical understanding of molecular systems, the development of novel systems to detect and quantify cell-cell interactions will accelerate the mapping of the interaction networks of multicellular systems.
evidence: This is an analogy-based argument for the importance of developing new tools.

claim: A suite of orthogonal baToN tools enables reciprocal cell-cell labeling, interaction-dependent cargo transfer, and the identification of higher order cell-cell interactions across a wide range of cell types.
source: A suite of orthogonal baToN tools enables reciprocal cell-cell labeling, interaction-dependent cargo transfer, and the identification of higher order cell-cell interactions across a wide range of cell types.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a summary of the system's capabilities.

claim: Recent studies have demonstrated a supportive role for neurons within the primary and metastatic niche in the context of brain.
source: Recent studies have demonstrated a supportive role for neurons within the primary and metastatic niche in the context of brain (Venkatesh et al., 2019; Zeng et al., 2019).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to recent literature.

claim: Transient labeling is sufficient to label stable cancer cell-stromal cell interactions when sender cells consistently express GFP.
source: Transient labeling is sufficient to label stable cancer cell-stromal cell interactions and many other diverse cell-cell interactions when sender cells consistently express GFP (Figure 1F).
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the kinetics data and system design.

claim: Transient labeling should allow dynamic interactions to be detected, ensuring that the labeled receiver cells either are in contact with, or have recently interacted with sender cells.
source: This transient labeling should allow dynamic interactions to be detected, ensuring that the labeled receiver cells either are in contact with, or have recently interacted with sender cells.
evidence: This is a logical inference based on the transient nature of the labeling.

claim: A G-baToN system where sGFP is inducible may allow physical interactions between cancer cells and stromal cells to be captured with even more precise temporal control.
source: For example, a G-baToN system where sGFP is inducible may allow physical interactions between cancer cells and stromal cells to be captured with even more precise temporal control.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about potential future improvements.

claim: It should be possible to develop systems that allow for stable receiver cell labeling through the transfer of site-specific recombinases or programmable nucleases to genetically modify receiver cells upon contact.
source: Finally, due to the intrinsic attribute of G-baToN as a cell-cell contact dependent cargo transfer system (Figure 8), it should be possible to develop systems that allow for stable receiver cell labeling, perhaps through the transfer of site-specific recombinases (e.g. Cre or FLP) or programmable nucleases (e.g. Cas9) to genetically modify receiver cells upon contact.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about potential future applications based on the cargo transfer capability.

claim: LIPSTIC-based labeling is driven by endogenous ligand-receptor interactions.
source: While LIPSTIC-based labeling is driven by endogenous ligand-receptor interactions, SynNotch and G-baToN systems rely on exogenous ligand-receptor pairs (Morsut et al., 2016; Pasqual et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a comparison statement supported by citations to the respective systems.

claim: SynNotch and G-baToN systems rely on exogenous ligand-receptor pairs.
source: While LIPSTIC-based labeling is driven by endogenous ligand-receptor interactions, SynNotch and G-baToN systems rely on exogenous ligand-receptor pairs (Morsut et al., 2016; Pasqual et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a comparison statement supported by citations.

claim: Tuning the affinity or expression level of the nanobody could minimize the effect of stabilizing normal cell-cell interactions.
source: It is possible that tuning the affinity or expression level of the nanobody could minimize this effect.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about potential optimization strategies.

claim: Inducible G-baToN systems may circumvent issues of stabilizing cell-cell interactions, thus ensuring the recording of only bona fide interactions.
source: Inducible G-baToN systems may circumvent these issues, thus ensuring the recording of only bona fide interactions.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about potential system improvements.

claim: A recent paper used secreted cell-permeable mCherry for proximity labeling of cells, but this system labels all cells in proximity and lacks true cell-cell interaction labeling.
source: A recent paper used secreted cell-permeable mCherry for proximity labeling of cells. This system circumvents the problem of abnormal cell-cell interactions caused by ligand-receptor binding; however, this system labels all cells in proximity and lacks true cell-cell interaction labeling (Ombrato et al., 2019).
